Safeguarding
Everyone at Chichester Nursery School works to help keep children safe from harm by providing a secure environment for children and their families.
Staff work closely with children and their families to build relationships, which result in a better ability to notice changes in behaviour and attitudes. With this knowledge we are able to provide support or take appropriate action to ensure all are kept safe, both at home and in the school.
The Designated Safeguarding Lead is Clare Blanchard, Head of School.
In her absence, the Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads are:
Jess Eaton, Up to 3s’ Manager
Claire May, Baby Room Lead
Ruth Campbell, Executive Head
If you have concerns about a child, you must:
If you have immediate concerns about a child’s safety you can contact Integrated Front Door on 01403 229 900 or out of hours on 0330 222 6664

Curriculum Goals
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Value, respect & communication skills
PSE encourages children to value themselves, respect difference in others and develop effective skills in communicating their thoughts and feelings.
Skilled and supportive adults are crucial to the effective delivery of PSE by promoting co-operative play and consideration to the needs of others as well as the important skill of negotiating as the children play and share toys.
We understand the importance of a warm supportive relationship with a key adult, someone who celebrates their successes and encourages them as they explore their environment and challenge themselves with new activities.
This subject doesn’t have a dedicated area in Nursery instead it goes on wherever the children are!
So PSE happens when children….
Share a drink or snack together
Communication & Language
Speaking, listening & attention and understanding
Communicating and being with others helps children to build social relationships which provide opportunities for friendship, empathy and sharing emotions. The ability to communicate helps children to participate more fully in society. Communication in the Foundation Stage is broken down in to three separate skills – speaking, listening and attention and understanding.
These are key components of the curriculum, as they form the foundations for literacy and all other areas of learning and we ensure these skills are developed throughout all activities in the Nursery School. Children develop their communication skills through everyday situations in Nursery, such as:
Asking for the things they want
Negotiating turns and ideas with other children
Literacy
Early reading and writing skills
As children develop speaking and listening skills they build the foundations for literacy, for making sense of visual and verbal signs and ultimately for reading and writing.
Children need lots of opportunities to interact with others as they develop these skills, and to use a wide variety of resources for expressing their understanding, including mark making, drawing, modelling, reading and writing.
We believe that children learn best through activities and experiences that engage all the senses. For example, music, dance and playing with rhythm, rhymes and songs play a key role in language development.
Physical development
Moving and handling
All children gain an understanding of the world around through movement and physical sensation. Physical development is learning about:
Controlling your body in space
Co-ordinating different parts of the body
Using fine movements to manipulate tools
Holding, threading, writing
Even keeping still!
Health and self care
Children are taught ways to keep healthy and safe, the importance of physical activity and healthy food choices, and how to manage basic hygiene and personal needs like dressing and going to the toilet independently.
All children have different needs, mastering skills at different rates and learning in different ways.
Carefully planned activities give time and opportunity for children to develop physical and self care skills with support, care and understanding, allowing them to gain confidence in their learning and their environment.
Mathematical development
Developing early mathematical skills
Through adult planned and child-initiated play opportunities we aim to give children a love of exploring mathematics and mathematical concepts. Development is supported in the following areas:
Counting and numeracy skills
Recognising and writing numerals
Developing mathematical strategies and problem solving
Understanding shape and space
Understanding and using mathematical language
Understanding the World
People and communities
With a starting point of their own particular personal history, children begin to develop an awareness of differences within families, communities and traditions. They begin to appreciate that other children may well have different likes and dislikes to themselves.
The World
Children initially learn about their most immediate surroundings, before developing their knowledge and experience of the wider environment. Through practical experiences they learn about objects, materials and living things.
Technology
Children gain confidence in handling a range of technology to support and enhance their learning.
Expressive Arts and Design
Expressive Arts and Design encourages children to use all their senses, take risks, think flexibly, play with ideas and respond imaginatively.
We believe that all children are creative and recognise that nurturing a child’s journey of curiosity, experimentation and forming personal choices is as important as any ‘end product’ they may produce.
Building interest and knowledge in Expressive Arts and Design will enable children to confidently use media and materials in resourceful ways and explore the diversity of their world and successfully express their ideas, feeling and views of it.

Links to useful SEND services
The links below are useful organisations, to support families :
Reaching Families is a parent-carer led, grassroots charity which aims to support parents and families of children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in their daily lives, in particular through the delivery of information, training and peer support.
We offer full-time, term-based provision, either in-person at Centres or at Red Balloon of the Air, which offers a hybrid of online and face-to-face support (up to 15 hours per week).
Our approach puts wellbeing at the core of our students’ education experience, with a strong emphasis on mental health, personal development and positive social interaction alongside academic teaching.
We help families in Sussex to overcome their difficulties and prevent crisis. We support families struggling with issues such as poverty, ill health, learning difficulties, bereavement, family break-up and domestic abuse.
WSPCF is an independent charity for the parent carers of children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND).
We support parent carers by providing information, signposting, and training that equips them in their lifelong caring role and empowers them to participate in shaping services for their children and young people.
We’re a clinician-led company that believes Autism and ADHD assessments should always be carried out in-person and to a high standard.
At Aspens we provide high quality care and support to people on the autism spectrum and with learning disabilities; and their families; meeting their needs and aspirations and empowering them to learn and grow through an integrated network of services across the South-East.

Fees & Funding
We understand that choosing the right nursery is an important decision for your family, and clarity around fees is a key part of that process.
At Chichester Nursery School, our fees reflect the high quality of care, education, and nurturing environment we provide for every child. They cover our experienced staff, carefully planned learning activities, and the resources that support your child’s development during their time with us.
Below you’ll find clear information about our session fees and any additional costs. If you have any questions or would like help understanding your childcare funding entitlement, we will be happy to assist.
Morning Session-09.00-12.00
After School Session-
(only applies to children attending a ‘long’ 9am-3pm day)
*Please note we do not charge for consumables, snack or nappies
Government Funded Hours (From 9 Months)
Chichester Nursery School is pleased to offer Government-funded childcare for eligible children from 9 months of age, helping families access high-quality early education from the very start of their child’s learning journey.
From the term after your child turns 9 months, eligible working families may be able to access 30 hours of funded childcare, depending on their circumstances. Funded hours are available during term time and can be used across a pattern of sessions, subject to availability. While the funding covers the cost of early education, additional charges may apply for hot meals or hours taken beyond the funded entitlement.
We are happy to guide you through the eligibility and application process, and answer any questions you may have, about how funded hours can be used at Chichester Nursery School. If you require more information on your entitlement, visit the Childcare choices tab below, or the admissions tab to contact admissions directly.

Using fresh and locally sourced ingredients, Little Tums offer a 3-week rolling menu, which doesn’t just offer a great variety of food but also meets the “Healthy Choice Award” guidelines that have been set out to the highest standard. Their menu plan has been awarded the highest Gold accreditation by being fully compliant with the recommended GDA’s and dietary requirements for children of nursery and school age.
The menus are designed in-house by a team of qualified chefs and then independently evaluated to ensure they meet the daily nutritional guidelines. Therefore, each child that receives a Little Tums meal is being provided a healthy, balanced and nutritious meal.
All children can access hot lunches, these are charged at £4.50 per meal. If you believe you are entitled to free school meals, please visit the Free School Meals section to apply.
Hot lunches
Little Tums' homemade hot lunches are all prepared on the day they are to be served, this ensure that each meal that is prepared, only contains ingredients that are fresh and tasty, ensuring quality and consistency throughout the meals.
Special dietary and cultural meals, make up a large percentage of the meals we prepare daily. Much care is taken into ensuring that they are prepared, in line with the children’s requirements. The dietary chefs take great pride in ensuring that their meals, are just as nutritionally balanced and tasty and therefore enjoyed. It is important that each child, regardless of their dietary, allergen or cultural needs has access to meals that are as similar as possible to our main menu.
All hot food is cooked to a minimum of 85 degrees centigrade, and once this minimum temperature is reached, the meals are packed into gastronorm containers. These are then sealed and labelled with the nursery name and allergen information. These are then packaged into hot holding thermo boxes which ensure your meals remain hot through transportation and arrive to you hot and ready to serve.

Governors
As a Local Authority Maintained Nursery School, we have a governing body in the same way that all other schools do.
Our governors come from various backgrounds, including staff members, parents and members of the local community with an interest in early years education. We are fortunate to have several governors from a teaching background which ensures that children's educational experiences are central to the work of the governing body. We also have governors with specific expertise in finance, community engagement and health and safety.
The governing body meet every half term to discuss and make decisions on matters such as finance, policies, staffing, resources, quality and standards and many other issues affecting the running of the Centre. Since the summer term 2017 the governors have decided that every meeting will involve the full governing body. This decision has removed the need for separate committee meetings, ensuring that information is shared more effectively across the whole governing body and providing coherent strategic oversight of the Centre.
​If you would like to contact a member of the governing body, please do so using the Chichester Nursery contact details.
You can view the current Governor pro forma , click the link below :
Ruth Campbell - Executive Head Teacher
Vikki Cripps - Head of School
​Sophie Elsdon - Chair of Governors & Local Authority Governor
​Abigail Blumzon - Vice Chair Co-opted
Abigail is a Chartered Project Manager and Fellow of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (FRICS), with over a decade of experience leading complex construction and building safety projects. She currently leads the South Coast Project Management team at a consultancy called Bailey Partnership and is passionate about creating safe, inclusive, and well-managed environments for communities.
As Vice Chair of Governors, Abigail brings a strong focus on strategic leadership, governance, and accountability. She is particularly interested in supporting staff development, ensuring robust health and safety practices, and strengthening the long-term sustainability of the Federation.
Abigail is also an active member of her local community and a parent, and is committed to ensuring that nursery settings provide nurturing, inclusive environments where every child can thrive.
Teresa Matthewson - Clerk to Governors
Clare Blanchard- Co-opted
Nicola Nield - Staff Governor
Nicola has been a Staff Governor since 2022 and has been part of the Boundstone team since 2013. She began her journey as a Nursery Nurse, working closely with children aged 3-4, supporting their early development and learning.
In 2024 Nicola took on a new post in the office as Finance Assistant, while still supporting in the nursery when needed. This dual role allows her to maintain a strong connection with both the operational and educational aspects of the setting.
This unique position supports Nicola to understand how the nursery operates from a range of perspectives and contribute effectively within the framework of the Governing Body.
​Angela Bradley- Co-opted
Angela became a Governor at the end of 2025. This is her first such role having undertaken a range of voluntary positions previously ranging from chairperson of homeowner’s associations to operating a hyperbaric chamber!
During the day Angela is a technical advisor to R&D projects working on malaria, principally in sub–Saharan Africa. She holds a PhD in Medical Entomology from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine and lived overseas for a large proportion of her career.
Previously she supported a vocational school in Uganda providing support both strategic and financial to staff, students and the charitable benefactors.
In recent years Angela has finally settled down as a wife and mother and enjoys the finer things in life, mainly her home and garden.
Vicki Ayles - Co-opted
Vicki began her role as Head of School at Bognor Regis Nursery School in January 2026. She has spent many years working as a Reception Teacher and Early Years Lead in primary schools across Arundel and Worthing, developing a deep commitment to high‑quality early childhood education.
Vicki enjoys reading and researching early childhood development, particularly in the areas of play‑based learning and inclusive practice. Outside of school, she loves spending time with her family and taking beach walks with their dog.
​Aedan Kerney- Co-opted
Aedan worked as a teacher in Lancing for forty-one years and in his retirement directs two local choirs. He became a governor at Boundstone Nursery School in 2009 and his own two children attended the Nursery in the 1970s. He is passionate about the importance of Early Years Education.

The Local Offer
Since September 2014, every Local Authority has been required to publish information about available services for children who have special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). This is known as the ‘Local Offer’. This easy to understand information will set out what is normally available in schools and early years settings (e.g. playgroups and day nurseries) to support children with additional needs. It is not simply a list of services, but provides useful information on how to access services, any eligibility criteria, how decisions are made and who makes them.
Additionally, as a Maintained School we are required to publish further information in a SEND report which can be found below.
Please click below to read about our own offer for children with additional needs or to go to the West Sussex County Council Local Offer website.
Our Special Needs Coordinator (SENCo) is Jess Davies and she can be contacted via email at: sen@chichesternursery.org or by phone on 01243 642959.
